manual_review_notes: Cream cheese into basket, then close the microwave: 2/5 fully reviewed successes. The original historical VCN86_002 and immediate parent CTR_196 each achieved 0/5 complete chains. The parent placed cheese in all five episodes but left the door ajar; its closest episode ended 2.72 degrees open. This candidate moves the whole microwave to a net translation [+0.550, -0.015, 0] m and yaw +35 degrees relative to VCN86_002, including the parent layout repair, and moves unused butter 12 cm in negative Y for clearance. The requested cheese and basket are unchanged. Each door starts fully open at -2.094 radians, and successful episodes close it through direct robot-door contact while preserving the placed cheese. CTR_205 and CTR_206 are two layout variants of the same Object + LIBERO10 composition, not separate semantic families. The changes are not an isolated causal comparison or a population-level success-rate estimate.

episode_reviews.notes: Reviewed all 94 decoded frames and the full 738-control trace. Cheese is deliberately grasped, carried and released into the basket; the robot then directly pushes the moving microwave door from fully open (-119.977 degrees) to native closed (+0.215347 degrees). Palm/hand contact with moving door geom g17 is recorded through controls 733-738. The released cheese continues sliding and rotating down inside the basket through its own settling: from control 200 it moves at most 1.758 cm and 27.30 degrees. The basket moves less than 0.36 micrometers. Every saved state from control 170 to the end was reconstructed without new controls: cheese contacts only the basket, and the basket contacts only cheese and its original floor; there is no later robot, door or other-object contact with either. From control 400 through 738 the cheese pose is constant to numerical precision. Native In stays true. This is its own release settling, not damage from the later door operation. The final five saved states 734-738 corroborate released, exact-basket-base supported and settled cheese. This is a read-only terminal audit of the ordinary ordered-native run, not a newly applied online gate or extended trajectory. Both final BDDL goals hold; no final TC gate.
